WARREN, N.J., Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- PTC Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ: PTCT) today announced that on Oct. 28, 2026, the company approved non-statutory stock options to purchase an aggregate of 9.620 shares of its common stock and 11,535 restricted stock units ("RSUs"), each representing the right to receive one share of its common stock upon vesting, to 13 new employees. The awards were made pursuant to the Nasdaq inducement grant exception as a component of the new hires' employment compensation.

The inducement grants were approved by PTC's Compensation Committee on Oct. 28, 2026, and are being made as an inducement material to each employee's acceptance of employment with the company in accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4).

All stock option awards have an exercise price of $63.02 per share, the closing price of PTC's common stock on Oct. 28, 2026, the date of the grant. The stock options each have a 10-year term and vest over four years, with 25% of the original number of shares vesting on the first anniversary of the applicable employee's new hire date and 6.25% of the original number of shares vesting at the end of each subsequent three-month period thereafter until fully vested, subject to the employee's continued service with the company through the applicable vesting dates. The RSUs each will vest over four years with 25% of the original number of shares vesting on each annual anniversary of the applicable employee's new hire date until fully vested, subject to the employee's continued service with the company through the applicable vesting dates.

DALLAS, Oct. 30, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- United States Lime & Minerals, Inc. (NASDAQ: USLM) today reported third quarter 2026 results: The Company’s revenues in the third quarter 2026 were $106.2 million, compared to $102.0 million in the third quarter 2025, an increase of $4.2 million, or 4.1%. For the first nine months 2026, the Company’s revenues were $293.1 million, compared to $284.8 million in the first nine months 2025, an increase of $8.4 million, or 2.9%. The increase in revenues in the third quarter 2026, compared to the third quarter 2025, resulted primarily from modest increases in both average sales prices and sales volumes. Increased sales volumes were principally due to increased demand from the Company’s steel customers, partially offset by reduced demand from the Company’s construction customers. The increase in revenues in the first nine months 2026, compared to the first nine months 2025, resulted primarily from modest increases in both average sales prices and sales volumes. Increased sales volumes were principally due to increased demand from the Company’s steel customers, partially offset by reduced demand from the Company’s roof shingle customers.

The Company’s gross profit was $50.8 million in the third quarter 2026, compared to $52.2 million in the third quarter 2025, a decrease of $1.4 million, or 2.7%. The Company’s gross profit was $139.2 million in the first nine months 2026, compared to $140.2 million in the first nine months 2025, a decrease of $1.0 million, or 0.7%. The decreases in gross profit in the third quarter and first nine months 2026, compared to the comparable 2025 periods, resulted primarily from higher transportation and fuel costs, driven principally by higher diesel costs, and production inefficiencies experienced during the integration of our new Texas kiln into our existing plant operations.

Selling, general and administrative (“SG&A”) expenses were $6.1 million in the third quarter 2026, compared to $5.9 million in the third quarter 2025, an increase of $0.1 million, or 2.3%. SG&A expenses were $18.1 million in the first nine months 2026, compared to $18.4 million in the first nine months 2025, a decrease of $0.3 million, or 1.5%.

Other (income) expense, net was $3.8 million and $10.4 million income in the third quarter and first nine months 2026, compared to $3.4 million and $9.6 million income in the third quarter and first nine months 2025, increases of $0.4 million and $0.8 million, respectively. The increases in other (income) expense, net for the third quarter and first nine months 2026, compared to the comparable 2025 periods, were primarily due to interest earned on higher average balances of cash and cash equivalents.

The Company reported net income of $38.0 million ($1.32 per share diluted) and $103.1 million ($3.58 per share diluted) in the third quarter and first nine months 2026, compared to $38.8 million ($1.35 per share diluted) and $103.7 million ($3.61 per share diluted) in the third quarter and first nine months 2025, decreases of $0.7 million, or 1.9%, and $0.6 million, or 0.6%, respectively.

“We saw modest increases in both volumes and sales prices for our lime and limestone products in the third quarter 2026, while our expenses reflected the impact of the sharp rise in diesel prices,” said Timothy W. Byrne, President and Chief Executive Officer. “Although we remain optimistic regarding overall construction demand in the future, certain large construction projects have recently experienced delays for various reasons, including securing permits, and we are monitoring indications that Texas’ residential construction is beginning to slow down. The new kiln at our Texas facility began intermittently producing quicklime in the third quarter, and we expect to have final commissioning completed in the fourth quarter. To that end, our costs in Texas have been impacted by production inefficiencies as we continue to integrate the new kiln into our existing plant operations,” Mr. Byrne added.

Dividend

The Company announced today that the Board of Directors has declared a regular quarterly cash dividend of $0.06 per share on the Company’s common stock. This dividend is payable on December 11, 2026 to stockholders of record at the close of business on November 20, 2026.

United States Lime & Minerals, Inc., a NASDAQ-listed public company with headquarters in Dallas, Texas, is a manufacturer of lime and limestone products, supplying primarily the construction (including highway, road, and building contractors), industrial (including paper and glass manufacturers), environmental (including municipal sanitation and water treatment facilities and flue gas treatment processes), metals (including steel producers), roof shingle manufacturers, agriculture (including poultry producers), and oil and gas services industries. The Company operates lime and limestone plants and distribution facilities in Arkansas, Colorado, Louisiana, Missouri, Oklahoma, and Texas through its wholly owned subsidiaries, Arkansas Lime Company, ART Quarry TRS LLC (DBA Carthage Crushed Limestone), Colorado Lime Company, Mill Creek Dolomite, LLC, Texas Lime Company, U.S. Lime Company, U.S. Lime Company-Shreveport, U.S. Lime Company-St. Clair, and U.S. Lime Company-Transportation. In addition, the Company, through its wholly owned subsidiary, U.S. Lime Company-O & G, LLC, has royalty and non-operated working interests in natural gas wells located in Johnson County, Texas, in the Barnett Shale Formation.

VIRGINIA BEACH, Va., Oct. 30, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- AH Realty Trust (NYSE: AHRT) today announced approximately 23,000 square feet of leasing activity across its Harbor Point community in Baltimore, Maryland, including four new leases, an expansion and a renewal. Harbor Point continues to command some of the highest office rents in the market, and following these transactions, the Company’s Harbor Point office portfolio is 98% leased.

“Tenants choose Harbor Point for what surrounds the office from the waterfront to the retail and restaurants,” said Shawn Tibbetts, Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer of AH Realty Trust. “The combination of new leasing, tenant expansion and renewal activity demonstrates our focus on attracting and retaining tenants, and the demand for communities like Harbor Point.”

At Thames Street Wharf, Arena Analytics signed a 1,700-square-foot lease with occupancy expected in November 2026. BluePath Finance leased nearly 5,000 square feet and took occupancy in September 2026.

At Wills Wharf, existing tenant Cole Schotz P.C. is relocating to a larger, nearly 9,000-square-foot space in the building, expanding its footprint by approximately 2,000 square feet. Law firm Zuckerman Spaeder LLP has leased Cole Schotz’s former nearly 7,000 square-foot space. Both tenants are expected to occupy their new space in mid-2027. RBC Royal Bank also renewed its lease for over 7,000 square feet.  

Located along Baltimore’s waterfront, Harbor Point combines Class A office space, retail, dining and residential uses in a mixed-use setting. AH Realty Trust’s holdings include the T. Rowe Price global headquarters, Thames Street Wharf, Wills Wharf and the Constellation Energy Building.

Financial Results for the Third Quarter 2026
Earnings

Net income for the third quarter 2026 was $7.1 million, a decrease of $0.26 million, or 3.6%, from the prior quarter, and an increase of $0.9 million, or 15.2%, from the prior year quarter. Diluted EPS decreased to $1.01 for the third quarter 2026 compared to $1.06 for the prior quarter and $0.88 for the prior year quarter.

Net Interest Income and Net Interest Margin

Net interest income for the third quarter 2026 was $19.3 million, an increase of $2.0 million from the prior quarter, and an increase of $2.4 million from the prior year quarter.

Interest income increased $1.8 million compared to the prior year quarter, driven primarily by higher rates on earning assets in the current quarter, while interest expense decreased $0.7 million compared to the prior year quarter due to lower costs on deposits. Net interest margin, on an FTE basis, was 4.41% for the current quarter, compared to 4.16% for the prior quarter, and 3.97% for the prior year quarter.

The yield earned on average loans held for investment increased to 6.42%, on an FTE basis, for the third quarter 2026, compared to 6.18% for the prior quarter and 6.12% for the prior year quarter.

The average cost of deposits was 2.13% for the third quarter 2026, compared to 2.13% for the prior quarter and 2.36% for the prior year quarter. Non-interest bearing demand deposits as a percent of total deposits was 26.6% as of September 30, 2026, compared to 28.0% and 27.8% at June 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025, respectively.

Non-interest Income

Total non-interest income for the third quarter 2026 was $3.7 million, a decrease of $1.7 million, or 31.1%, from the prior quarter, and no change from the prior year quarter. The decrease during the quarter was primarily due the recognition of a gain on the sale of a bank administrative office that was no longer being used in the prior quarter that did not recur during the third quarter 2026.  

Non-interest Expense

Total non-interest expense for the third quarter 2026 was $14.9 million, an increase of $1.2 million, or 8.7%, from the prior quarter, and an increase of $2.1 million, or 16.6%, from the prior year quarter.

The third quarter 2026 efficiency ratio was 65.00% compared to 60.73% and 62.30% for the prior quarter and prior year quarter, respectively. The improvement in the current quarter compared to the prior year quarter was primarily due to higher net interest margin and an increase in non-interest income.

Acquisition related expenses for the third quarter 2026 was $2.0 million, an increase of $1.4 million, or 251.2%, from the prior quarter. No acquisition related expenses were paid in the prior year quarter.

Income Taxes

Total income tax provision expense for the third quarter 2026 was $0.8 million, a decrease of $0.8 million, or 51.1%, from the prior quarter, and a decrease of $0.6 million, or 42.2%, from the prior year quarter, reflecting an effective tax rate of 10.0%, 17.96%,and 18.1%, respectively. The decrease in the effective tax rate during the third quarter 2026 was due to the utilization of federal income tax credits purchased at a discount which reduced tax expense during the quarter.

Loans

Loans held for investment increased $273.8 million, or 19.3%, to $1.69 billion as of September 30, 2026 compared to June 30, 2026, and increased $176.1 million, or 11.6% from September 30, 2025. The increases are mainly attributed to the acquisition of FSC Bancshares, Inc.

Investments

Investments increased $41.7 million, or 17.7%, to $277.9 million as of September 30, 2026 compared to June 30, 2026, and increased $51.9 million, or 23.0%, from September 30, 2025. The increases are mainly attributed to the acquisition of FSC Bancshares, Inc.

Asset Quality

Non-performing assets to total loans was 0.59% at September 30, 2026, 0.53% at June 30, 2026, and 0.48% at September 30, 2025. Non-performing assets totaled $9.9 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $7.5 million and $7.3 million at June 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025, respectively. The increase in the current year quarter compared to the prior year quarter was due to an increase in non-accrual loans within the commercial loan segment.

In the third quarter 2026, the Company had net loan charge-offs of $0.07 million, or 0.02% annualized, of average loans, compared to net loan charge-offs of $0.14 million, or 0.04% of average loans, and $0.04 million, or 0.01% annualized, of average loans, in the prior quarter and prior year quarter, respectively.

The Company provided a provision for credit losses of $0.3 million for the third quarter 2026 compared to providing a $0.2 million provision in the prior quarter, and providing a $0.4 million provision for the prior year quarter.

The allowance for credit losses at September 30, 2026 was $24.4 million, or 1.45% of outstanding loans, and 248.71% of non-performing loans. At June 30, 2026, the allowance for credit losses was $20.7 million, or 1.46% of outstanding loans, and 311.50% of non-performing loans. At September 30, 2025, the allowance for credit losses was $21.9 million, or 1.45% of outstanding loans, and 446.02% of non-performing loans. The allowance for credit losses represents management’s best estimate of expected losses inherent in the loan portfolio and is commensurate with risks in the loan portfolio as of September 30, 2026 as determined by management. The increase in the current quarter is largely driven by the Day 1 allowance for credit losses recorded in conjunction with the acquisition of FSC Bancshares, Inc.

Deposits

Total deposits at September 30, 2026 were $1.79 billion, an increase of $302.8 million, or 20.3%, from June 30, 2026, and an increase of $265.0 million, or 17.4% annualized, from September 30, 2025. The increases were mainly attributed to the acquisition of FSC Bancshares, Inc.

Capital

The Company maintains its “well capitalized” regulatory capital position. At September 30, 2026, capital ratios were as follows: total risk-based capital to risk-weighted assets 14.29%; tier 1 capital to risk-weighted assets 13.04%; common equity tier 1 10.15%; tier 1 leverage 12.59%; and common equity to assets 8.92%.

Pursuant to the Company's Repurchase Plan, management is given discretion to determine the number and pricing of the shares to be purchased under the plan, as well as the timing of any such purchases. The Board of Directors amended the plan on July 29, 2026 to increase the authorized repurchase limit to $10 million. The Company repurchased 12,000 common shares under the repurchase plan during the first nine months of 2026 at an average cost of $32.68 per share totaling $0.4 million. As of September 30, 2026, $10.0 million remains available for share repurchases pursuant to the plan.

 On October 30, 2026, the Company's Board of Directors approved a quarterly cash dividend of $0.21 per common share, payable January 1, 2027 to shareholders of record at the close of business on December 15, 2026.

Merger with FSC Bancshares, Inc.

On September 3, 2026, the Company completed its acquisition of FSC Bancshares, Inc. and its wholly owned subsidiary, Farmers State Bank (collectively, “FSC”) whereby FSC Bancshares, Inc. was merged with and into Hawthorn Bancshares, Inc. and Farmers State Bank was merged with and into Hawthorn Bank. Pursuant to the merger agreement executed on April 29, 2026, the Company paid $17.0 million of cash consideration and issued 413,042 shares of Company stock. The Company and the Bank assumed all of the assets and liabilities of the FSC entities with which they merged by operation of law. The acquisition added 9 full-service branch locations located in northern Missouri.

Farmers State Bank's results of operations were included in Hawthorn's consolidated results of operations beginning September 3, 2026. Hawthorn will operate Farmers State Bank as a separate division of Hawthorn Bank until it is merges with and into Hawthorn Bank, which is expected to occur in March 2027.

NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Arch Insurance North America (Arch Insurance, Arch), today announced it has entered into an agreement to acquire Premier Dealer Holding Corp., and its subsidiaries including Premier Dealer Services (PDS), a Dublin, Ohio-based provider of automotive Finance and Insurance (F&I) products and services.

The acquisition, upon completion, will build on a long-standing relationship between Arch Insurance and PDS, combining Arch’s deep specialty insurance expertise with PDS’s administration capabilities, technology infrastructure and relationships.

“PDS has built a strong business with an experienced team, differentiated technology and extensive dealer relationships,” said Matt Shulman, CEO of Arch Insurance North America. “We know the company well. Bringing PDS and Arch together will strengthen our capabilities in the automotive F&I market and create new opportunities to serve our customers and partners.”

“Arch has been a trusted partner to Premier for many years, and we know and respect their team,” said John Topits, CEO of PDS. “Joining Arch gives us the financial strength and resources to keep investing in our people, products and technology, while our dealers and agents continue working with the same Premier team they know today.”

Following completion of the transaction, PDS is expected to operate as a standalone business within Arch Insurance’s Consumer Division.

This transaction is expected to close by the end of 2026 and is subject to regulatory approvals and satisfaction of other customary closing conditions.

TD Securities is acting as the exclusive financial advisor to Arch, and Eversheds Sutherland LLP is serving as Arch’s legal advisor.

About Arch Insurance North America

Arch Insurance North America, part of Arch Capital Group Ltd., includes Arch’s insurance operations in the United States and Canada. Business in the U.S. is written by Arch Insurance Company, Arch Specialty Insurance Company, Arch Property & Casualty Insurance Company and Arch Indemnity Insurance Company. BERWICK, Pa.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--First Keystone Corporation (OTCID: FKYS), parent company of First Keystone Community Bank, reported an increase in total interest income of $3,195,000 or 5.6%, as compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was predominantly due to interest earned on increased balances of interest-bearing deposits held at the Federal Reserve Bank compared to the same period in 2025. Total interest expense increased by $957,000 or 3.3% overall, mainly due to an increase of $675,000 in interest expense related to interest paid on the Bank’s outstanding subordinated debt due to the contracted change from fixed to floating rate which transpired in 2026. The rate paid on the subordinated debt increased from 4.375% fixed to a floating rate which was equivalent to 7.745% as of the September 30, 2026 interest payment. The net effect of derivative agreements decreased net interest income by $809,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and increased net interest income by $586,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. These derivative agreements are part of the Corporation’s interest rate risk management strategy and are intended to mitigate exposure to changes in market interest rates. The provision for credit losses for the nine month period decreased by $1,894,000 to a recovery of credit losses of $1,125,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to expense of $769,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The recovery of credit losses for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was mainly the result of a decrease of $640,000 in the provision for credit losses related to the Bank’s owner-occupied, non-farm, non-residential loans. Of the $640,000, a decrease of $440,000 was due to a reduction in specific allocation on an individually evaluated loan and a decrease of $200,000 was attributable to a decrease in the outstanding principal balance of owner-occupied, non-farm, non-residential loans of $1,954,000, along with a decrease in the related quantitative loss rate. The Bank also experienced decreases in outstanding principal balance and quantitative loss rates related to pooled/collectively evaluated loans in two of the Bank’s larger loan categories: multifamily loans and non-owner occupied, non-farm, non-residential loans. The outstanding principal balance of pooled/collectively evaluated loans related to these two categories decreased by $7,659,000 and $3,710,000 during the nine months ended September 30, 2026. The provision for credit losses related to these categories decreased by $329,000 and $189,000, respectively as of the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

Non-interest income increased by $594,000 or 10.9% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the same period in 2025. Net securities gains improved by $537,000 to a gain of $665,000 compared to a gain of $128,000 as a result of changes in the mark-to-market adjustment on held equity securities. Other non-interest income decreased $201,000 mainly due to $255,000 in gains from life insurance proceeds realized from a death benefit received during the first nine months of 2025, offset by a recovery of $49,000 on a prior defalcation loss, an increase of $45,000 in ATM and debit card fees, and an increase of $30,000 in income related to bank owned life insurance recorded during the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

Non-interest expense increased by $1,309,000 or 5.3% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the same period in 2025. The increase was mainly due to a $605,000 increase in salaries and employee benefits, a $444,000 increase in professional services expense, a $366,000 increase in furniture, equipment and computers expense, an increase of $90,000 in ATM and debit card expenses, and an increase of $88,000 in data processing fees, offset by a decrease of $307,000 in other non-interest expense related to a fraud write off associated with a customer account realized in the first quarter of 2025.

Net income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $9,475,000. Net income per share was $1.50 while dividends totaled $0.84 per share for the nine months ended September 30, 2026. Net income increased by $2,700,000 or 39.9% as compared to the same period in 2025. The increase was primarily due to increased interest income and a decrease in the provision for credit losses.

Total assets increased to $1,726,469,000 at September 30, 2026, an increase of $144,092,000 or 9.1% as compared to September 30, 2025. Cash and cash equivalents increased by $184,869,000 or 125.5% as compared to September 30, 2025 mainly due to increased deposit balances during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, offset with a decrease in the balance of securities and restricted stocks, as discussed below, and a decrease in the balance of loans which resulted from regular principal payments and paydowns outpacing new loan originations for the nine months ended September 30, 2026. Securities and restricted stocks decreased $34,082,000 or 8.1% as compared to September 30, 2025 mainly due to a decrease in securities balances of $34,877,000 which resulted from $64,025,000 in maturities, calls, and paydowns and a decline of $9,718,000 in the fair value adjustment on securities between September 30, 2025 and September 30, 2026, offset by investment purchases of $42,598,000 in 2026. Deposits increased by $123,299,000 or 10.3% at September 30, 2026 as compared to September 30, 2025 due to increases in retail CDs offset with decreases in other retail deposits and brokered CDs. Stockholders’ equity increased $1,012,000 or 0.9% mainly due to increases in retained earnings and surplus of $1,813,000 and $1,233,000, respectively, offset by an increase of $2,187,000 in accumulated other comprehensive loss.

ELMER, N.J.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--ELMER BANCORP, INC. (“Elmer Bancorp” or the “Company”) (OTCID: ELMA), the parent company of The First National Bank of Elmer (the “Bank”), announces its operating results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, Elmer Bancorp reported net income of $786,000, or $0.68 per average diluted common share, compared to $768,000, or $0.67 per average diluted common share for the three months ended September 30, 2025. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, net income totaled $2.195 million or $1.91 per average diluted common share compared to $2.584 million, or $2.26 per average diluted common share for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

Net interest income for the three months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $4.245 million, an increase of $134,000 from $4.111 million in the third quarter of 2025. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, net interest income totaled $12.530 million compared to $11.893 million for the nine-month period of 2025. This increase in net interest income is the result of higher interest and fees on loans and lower interest paid on deposits partially offset by lower income on our overnight investments. The loan loss provision was increased by $70,000 and $160,000 for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to an increase of $40,000 and $124,000 for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025. This adjustment was the result of the required loan loss calculation under the Current Expected Credit Loss (“CECL”) model.

Non-interest income for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $36,000 higher than the same three-month period a year ago and $461,000 lower than the nine-month period last year. Increases in Visa credit card commissions and higher service fee income accounted for the increase in the three-month period. The decrease in the nine-month period was the result of the one-time “BOLI” payout of $530,000 received in the first quarter of 2025 partially offset by higher service fee income.

Non-interest expenses were higher for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 versus the prior year periods by $120,000 and $491,000, respectively. Increases in employment costs, occupancy and equipment costs and data processing costs were partially offset by lower professional fees.

Elmer Bancorp’s total assets at September 30, 2026 totaled $398.1 million, a decrease of $12.1 million from the September 30, 2025 level of $410.2 million. Loans totaled $339.7 million at September 30, 2026, an increase of $16.5 million from the September 30, 2025 total of $323.2 million. This increase in loans was more than offset by a decrease in overnight investments of $25.4 million. At September 30, 2026, the allowance for loan losses was 1.27% of total loans.

Deposits totaled $354.6 million at September 30, 2026, compared to the September 30, 2025 total of $369.2 million, reflecting a decrease of $10.5 million in interest bearing deposits and a decrease of $4.1 million in non-interest-bearing deposits. The September 30, 2025 balance included $5.0 million in short term borrowings which have since been re-paid and outlier deposit fluctuations of several large clients. In addition, the collection and growth of deposits continues to be highly competitive and rate sensitive. Stockholders’ equity totaled $40.8 million at September 30, 2026. The book value per share at September 30, 2026 was $35.23 compared to $33.36 per share at September 30, 2025. The Bank met all regulatory capital requirements to be classified as a well-capitalized institution as of September 30, 2026.

Brian W. Jones, President and Chief Executive Officer stated, “Our third quarter results remain strong highlighted by our solid loan growth of $16.5 million year-over-year. Net income continues to be consistent and at sustained levels. We remain confident in our ability to drive value for our shareholders as we continue to build shareholder equity. As always, we would like to thank our customers, shareholders and employees for their steadfast support.”

The First National Bank of Elmer, a nationally chartered bank headquartered in Elmer, New Jersey, has a long history of serving the community since its beginnings in 1903. We are a community bank focused on providing deposit and loan products to retail customers and to small and mid-sized businesses from our six full-service branch offices located in Cumberland, Gloucester and Salem Counties, New Jersey, including our main office located at 10 South Main Street in Elmer, New Jersey. In addition to our branch offices, the bank also operates a loan production office (“LPO”) located in Marlton, NJ to service our clients in Burlington County. Deposits at The First National Bank of Elmer are insured up to the legal maximum amount by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (“FDIC”).
